'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**An [[International Rescue Committee]] staff member and three [[Danish Refugee Council]] aid workers are shot dead in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Tigray Region]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/12/11/four-humanitarian-workers-killed-tigray-aid-agencies-struggle/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*The [[BW Group]] says the crew of one of their ships saw an [[oil tanker]] suffer an explosion after being hit by "an external source" off the coast of [[Jeddah]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. They also say that oil may have leaked from the site of the blast. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/explosion-hits-ship-off-saudi-red-sea-port-of-jiddah/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Italy|Italian]] intellectuals [[Corrado Augias]] and [[Giovanna Melandri]] hand back their medals of the [[Legion of Honour]], [[France]]'s highest [[order of merit]], to France. They protest the news that [[President of Egypt]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] was awarded the [[Grand Cross]] of the Legion at the same time that prosecutors in [[Rome]] indicted four top security officials of the Sisi regime over the 2016 [[Murder of Giulio Regeni|abduction and torture to death of Giulio Regeni]], an Italian doctoral student, in [[Cairo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-abdel-fattah-el-sissi-italy-giulio-regeni-egypt-661099fa0f952b856be54d96203db3eb (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020–21 South Pacific cyclone season]]
**[[Cyclone]]s [[Cyclone Yasa|Yasa]] and Zazu threaten several [[Pacific]] countries, especially [[Fiji]]. Yasa intensifies into a category 2 storm, remaining in the waters between Fiji and [[Vanuatu]]. It is expected to reach Fiji on Thursday as a category 4 storm. Zazu also brings heavy rains to [[Tonga]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/432842/dual-cyclones-threaten-to-menace-several-pacific-countries (RNZ)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death toll]] from [[COVID-19]] in the United States exceeds 300,000. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/14/health/us-covid-deaths-300k/index.html (CNN)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****The [[United States]] begins administering their first doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. Sandra Lindsay, a nurse at the [[Long Island Jewish Medical Center]] in [[New York (state)|New York]], becomes the first person in the country to receive the vaccine outside of a clinical trial. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/us-administer-1st-doses-pfizer-coronavirus-vaccine/story?id=74703018 (ABC News)]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in West Virginia]]
******[[Governor of West Virginia|Governor]] [[Jim Justice]] becomes one of the first elected officials to receive the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.stltoday.com/news/state-and-regional/missouri/west-virginia-governor-is-among-1st-to-get-vaccine/article_c2783bd6-2243-57c5-83df-944b4c14504f.html (''St. Louis Post-Dispatch'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
*****[[Mayor of Boston|Boston Mayor]] [[Marty Walsh (politician)|Marty Walsh]] announces that the [[Boston|city]] will rollback to phase 2 and tighten their restrictions as an effort to stop the spread of COVID-19. [https://apnews.com/article/museums-boston-coronavirus-pandemic-947cd07b7453d6b5ba547ca5273b853e (AP)] [https://www.wcvb.com/article/boston-coronavirus-covid-mayor-walsh-economic-rollback-december-14-2020/34965702 (WCVB-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
*****[[Canada]] begins administering the vaccine to healthcare workers and elderly nursing home residents. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-canada-vaccine-idINKBN28O17B (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|Health Secretary]] [[Matt Hancock]] announces that [[London]] and parts of [[Essex]] and [[Hertfordshire]] will move into the highest level "Tier 3" restrictions on December 16 at 00:01 a.m. [[GMT]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-london-to-move-into-tier-3-restrictions-imminently-matt-hancock-tells-mps-12161363 (Sky News)]
*****The [[United Kingdom]] discovers a [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|new variant]] of [[COVID-19]] which is growing faster in some parts of [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-55308211 (BBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Mark Rutte]] imposes a tough five-week nationwide lockdown. Schools, museums, gyms and all non-essential shops, will be closed from midnight until January 19. [https://apnews.com/article/international-news-mark-rutte-netherlands-coronavirus-pandemic-restaurants-62f528f5c0350abcdeb20e6214e04cdb (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces that [[Turkey|the country]] will impose a five-day full [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] from December 31 at 9:00 p.m. local time until January 4, as a record 229 deaths were reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1777306/world (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]]
*****[[Delhi]] surpasses 10,000 total deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.indiatoday.in/coronavirus-outbreak/story/delhi-coronavirus-covid19-bulletin-dec-13-death-toll-new-cases-positivity-rate-1749222-2020-12-13 (India Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]] announces that the Go To Travel campaign will be suspended nationwide from December 28 to January 11. He also says that [[Tokyo]] and [[Nagoya]] will be removed as eligible destinations for the campaign. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/12/14/national/suga-go-to-travel-coronavirus/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Prime Minister of Singapore|Prime Minister]] [[Lee Hsien Loong]] says that [[Singapore]] has approved the [[Pfizer]]-[[BioNTech]] [[Tozinameran|vaccine]]. The country expects to receive shipments of the vaccine by the end of the year and to [[vaccination|vaccinate]] 5.7 million people for free by the third quarter of 2021. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/14/singapore-approves-pfizers-covid-vaccine.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] orders schools in the [[Seoul Capital Area]] to close from tomorrow until the end of the month due to an increase in new COVID-19 cases, which has broken records not seen since the [[pandemic]] began. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/south-korea-orders-schools-to-shut-as-covid-19-cases-spike-13768064 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[President of South Africa|President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] announces that public gatherings will be limited to no more than 100 people for indoor events and 250 people for outdoor events, and that the nationwide [[curfew]] will be extended from 11:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. throughout the holiday season. He also said that alcohol will only be sold from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. local time, Monday to Thursday. [https://www.iol.co.za/news/politics/ramaphosa-announces-new-curfew-restrictions-on-alcohol-and-public-gatherings--58266986-7ca2-4df1-9a15-4a2a222f9666 (Independent Online)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Sudan–United States relations]], [[War on terror|Global war on terrorism]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces that the United States has removed [[Sudan]] from the list of [[state sponsors of terrorism]]. Sudan had recently paid a $335 million settlement to the US government for US victims of terrorist attacks. [https://www.reuters.com/article/sudan-usa/u-s-to-remove-sudan-from-terrorism-list-on-monday-embassy-idUSKBN28O0TG?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Turkey–United States relations]], [[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act|CAATSA]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces that the United States has imposed sanctions on [[Turkey]] over its acquisition of the [[S-400 missile system|S-400 missile defense system]] from [[Russia]]. This move is the first time that the CAATSA has been used to penalize a U.S. ally. [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-politics-turkey-ankara-russia-c77d08a1ec06ebb3dae99bb05a67191b (AP)]
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]] bans the launching of [[propaganda]] leaflets into [[North Korea]]. The [[balloon propaganda campaigns in Korea|balloon propaganda campaigns]] have been used by [[North Korean defectors]] and [[Korean reunification]] activists for decades to spread anti-government propaganda, news from the outside world that is restricted in the North, money, food, and USB flash drives containing South Korean media. The ban also outlaws the use of loudspeaker propaganda broadcasts. Violators of the ban will face up to three years in prison or 30 million won ([[$]]27,400) in fines. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-southkorea/south-korea-bans-anti-north-leaflets-defector-says-he-wont-stop-idUSKBN28O1OI (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Singapore]]
**The [[judicial commissioner]] of [[Singapore]] sentences a [[Bangladesh]]i national to death after he was found guilty of [[murder|murdering]] his [[Indonesians|Indonesian]] girlfriend two years ago. In Singapore, a charge of murder carries the mandatory [[death penalty]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/courts-crime/man-sentenced-to-death-for-killing-girlfriend-after-she-refused-to-stop (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**The [[United States Electoral College|Electoral College]] meets in the state capitals to officially elect the next [[President of the United States|President]]. [[Joe Biden]], the presumptive [[president-elect of the United States|president-elect]], is officially elected president after securing [[California]]'s 55 electoral votes and will be [[inauguration of Joe Biden|inaugurated]] on January 20. Outgoing [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] continues to [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election|dispute]] the results of the election, claiming widespread [[electoral fraud]], despite [[Post-election lawsuits related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election|numerous failed lawsuits]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2020/dec/14/electoral-college-joe-biden-us-election-donald-trump-coronavirus-covid-19-pfizer-vaccine-russia-hackers-live-updates (''The Guardian'')]
**[[2020 United States presidential election in Michigan]]
***The [[Michigan State Capitol]] is closed to the public for the day and its [[Michigan Legislature|legislative]] sessions are cancelled due to "credible threats of violence" in response to the election. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/12/14/politics/michigan-state-house-and-senate-closed-threats/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Republican reactions to Donald Trump's claims of 2020 election fraud]]
***Outgoing [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Paul Mitchell (politician)|Paul Mitchell]] announces that he has left the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] to become a [[Third-party and independent members of the United States Congress|independent]] over outgoing [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s voter fraud claims and attempts to overturn the results. [https://abcnews.com/Politics/michigan-rep-paul-mitchell-quits-republican-party-trumps/story?id=74725718 (ABC News)]
*[[List of dismissals and resignations in the first Trump administration|List of Trump administration dismissals and resignations]]
**Outgoing President Donald Trump announces that [[William Barr]] will resign as [[United States Attorney General]] on December 23. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/14/attorney-general-william-barr-resigns-effective-dec-23.html (CNBC)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Solar eclipse of December 14, 2020]]
** A [[Solar eclipse#Total eclipse|total solar eclipse]] is seen in [[Chile]], [[Argentina]], and the [[South Pacific Ocean]]. [https://eclipsewise.com/solar/SEprime/2001-2100/SE2020Dec14Tprime.html (EclipseWise)]
*Several [[Google]] services go down without warning around 11:50 [[UTC]], including [[YouTube]], [[Google Search]], and the [[Google Play]] Store. The chatting [[Application software|app]] [[Discord (software)|Discord]] and mobile video game ''[[Pokémon Go]]'' also go down. The cause was revealed to be an “authentication system outage” by the Google Cloud [[Twitter]] account. [https://www.ign.com/articles/google-services-go-down-gmail-youtube-and-more-offline (IGN)] [https://www.newsweek.com/google-down-offline-gmail-youtube-calendar-drive-hangouts-not-working-problem-1554517 (''Newsweek'')]
*Amid controversy over alleged illegal content, [[Pornhub]] removes all non-verified user-uploaded videos, which make up the majority of the videos on the platform. Pornhub says that its new measures are now "more strict than any [[social media]] platform". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-55304115 (BBC News)]
